QatarEnergy Emerges from Insolvency, Resumes Oil and Gas Operations

DOHA, June 20—QatarEnergy, one of Qatar’s largest oil and gas producers, has exited insolvency proceedings, allowing production and exports to resume after a turbulent period that disrupted energy markets and raised concerns about the country’s economic outlook.

The company was declared insolvent in late May, with court filings citing “cash flow constraints arising from contract disputes and delayed receivables.” The move marked the most significant insolvency in the Gulf energy sector in over a decade, temporarily halting QatarEnergy’s upstream and downstream operations, including liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments, refinery activities, and domestic fuel supply.

After extensive negotiations with creditors and government agencies, QatarEnergy announced on Tuesday that it had completed a court-supervised restructuring. Under the terms of the agreement, the state provided a capital injection while major creditors, including Al Safwa Finance, agreed to debt rescheduling. Operations restarted on June 18, with the company confirming that LNG exports from Ras Laffan and Mesaieed had resumed.

“We are grateful for the swift and decisive support from the government and our partners, which has enabled us to stabilize our operations and restore confidence,” said Nasser Al-Kuwari, QatarEnergy’s acting CEO. “Our workforce has returned, and we are prioritizing safety and efficiency as we ramp up to full capacity.”

Analysts say the insolvency briefly reduced Qatari oil and gas exports by up to 15%, disrupting global supply chains and prompting price spikes in Asia and Europe. “This episode was a wake-up call for the sector,” said Rana Faris, an energy analyst at Doha-based Gulf Markets Insight. “It exposed vulnerabilities in payment systems and the need for greater financial oversight.”

The Qatar Oil and Gas Workers Union welcomed the company’s emergence from insolvency, noting that around 3,500 employees had faced uncertainty during the shutdown. “We are relieved that jobs have been protected and operations are back on track,” union president Khalid Hassan said.

With the restructuring completed, QatarEnergy pledged to strengthen its risk management and improve transparency. The Ministry of Energy stated that “Qatar’s energy sector remains robust,” and said it would work closely with QatarEnergy to prevent similar disruptions in future.

The company is expected to issue a detailed recovery plan later this month as it seeks to reassure global markets and stakeholders.
